note: For every check the verifier classifies as `none`, what we looked for before saying we invented it. A check with no external basis is not a defect, but an unexamined `none` is: it means we stopped looking and called the result our design. Each entry records the searches, the nearest neighbour found, and why it did not cover the rule.

checks.name: package structure

searches.query: SCITT agent receipt package file layout manifest requirement
searches.result: The drafts in basis/sources.json specify receipt payload fields, not a package's file layout. Nothing found stating which files a receipt package must contain.

nearest.why_not: It constrains the protected header and payload, not a directory of files.

checks.note: Our rule (declared files present, no extras) stays ours.

checks.name: evidence integrity

searches.query: content hash tamper evidence requirement receipt package
searches.result: Hashing content is universal practice; no external text requires it of an agent-evidence package in the way we frame it, and the symlink fence is plainly ours.

nearest.why_not: It requires digests of closure components, which is S10, not of package files.

checks.note: Half the rule is common practice, half is our hardening; neither is a published requirement.

checks.name: evidence index metadata

searches.query: C2PA hard binding manifest metadata digest exclude
searches.result: C2PA requires a hard binding from manifest to asset content, and at most one of them. That binds content to manifest; it does not require that a package's index metadata carry a digest of its own, separate from the content hashes it lists.

searches.query: agent receipt index digest metadata not covered by content hash
searches.result: No hit in the drafts we have cached; the closest statements are about closure components (S10) and chain links (S17), both of which are about different objects.

searches.query: IETF draft agent receipt manifest digest over metadata evidence index integrity 2026
searches.result: No IETF text. One practitioner repository (getaskclaw/multi-agent-dialogue-protocol, issue #5) already builds an evidence-index canary whose tamper flips both a report and a validator independently. The idea is not novel; the normative sentence is what is missing.

prior_art.what: an evidence index derived on demand, with a tamper canary that fails the report and the validator independently
prior_art.why_it_does_not_settle_it: a repository is not a requirement; nothing there obliges anyone else to cover the index

nearest.doc: C2PA hard binding (via streaming-video-technology-alliance CML results page)
nearest.why_not: A hard binding binds an asset's bytes to a manifest. Our gap is a manifest's own metadata, which no content hash covers, so editing it leaves every check green. Different direction, different object.

checks.note: This is the D-002 defect turned into a proposal: the sentence that survived an edit is the sentence nobody hashed. Prior art found the same day it was written, so the draft says so rather than presenting the idea as ours.

checks.name: timestamp and identifier strictness

searches.query: SCITT receipt MUST sequence_number monotonic reject replay
searches.result: draft-chang-delta1-settlement-00 §7.1 requires run_id nonces that the validator MUST reject on reuse, and §7.2 requires a strictly increasing sequence_number per validator instance.

searches.query: agent session receipt seq issued_at field requirements
searches.result: draft-bailey-scitt-agent-session-receipt requires each receipt to carry seq (0-based contiguous) and issued_at (RFC 3339 UTC).

nearest.why_not: The documents constrain the fields' meaning; they do not tell a verifier to reject impossible values on sight. That refusal is ours - which is exactly what `related` means.

checks.note: We had been saying 'nothing requires this' while the two field-level requirements sat in drafts we already cite elsewhere in basis. Reclassifying S12 to `related` needs a verifier change, tracked upstream.

checks.name: anchor event resolution

searches.query: OpenTimestamps verification resolve block merkle root mismatch semantics draft
searches.result: draft-crovia-tacet-01 states: "A verifier that cannot reach a header source MUST report the anchor as unchecked, never as failed, and MUST expose the height and the expected Merkle root so that a human can check them elsewhere." draft-fassbender-scitt-time-anchor-07 says a branch whose replay cannot complete returns NULL, and "Section 3.1 step 8 classifies the branch as unevaluated rather than as failing."

searches.query: anchor event resolution verifier requirement recompute root
searches.result: fassbender-07 also constrains the replay itself: append, prepend and SHA-256 only. The three-state reporting this repo was about to propose is already normative in two drafts.

nearest.why_not: It scopes OTS-style header anchors. Our rule also resolves a non-header anchor (a SCITT time-stamp token), and the order in which anchor types are tried is ours - which is why this is `related` rather than `direct`.

checks.note: p-002 was drafted today and withdrawn the same day: the survey it asked for had already been answered, twice, with MUST. Filing it would have been exactly the overclaim this table exists to prevent, so the withdrawal is recorded in the file rather than deleted.
